subject: Ancient Greek art
hook: ANCIENT GREEK ART IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Ancient Greek pottery was not primarily made for everyday use, but was largely mass-produced as a cheaper substitute for metalware to be placed in graves.
angle_support: In recent decades many scholars have questioned this, seeing much more production than was formerly thought as made to be placed in graves, as a cheaper substitute for metalware in both Greece and Etruria.
Pottery was the main form of grave goods deposited in tombs, often as "funerary urns" containing the cremated ashes, and was widely exported.
title: Why Ancient Greek Pottery Is Mostly Fakes
description: Ancient Greek pottery is often viewed as everyday kitchenware, but evidence suggests these vessels were mass-produced as affordable metal substitutes for funerary rites.
narration: ANCIENT GREEK ART IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture these painted vessels in everyday Greek homes. It was closer to a mass-produced, budget-friendly alternative to expensive metalware, specifically manufactured to be buried in tombs. By the fifth century BC, production became an industrial process. Instead of domestic utility, vast quantities were crafted as affordable grave goods. These ceramic substitutes allowed families to honor the dead without the cost of bronze. Clay was simply the cheaper way to bury the elite.
